description: Coordinator-requested investigation of the azulene_type_nonalternant cluster (49/84), the second-largest cluster from the K2b 84-molecule diagnosis. NOT boundable within this PR -- report only, no code change.
verdict: NOT boundable in this PR. Requires a fundamentally different Pass-1/Pass-2 architecture (whole-fused-system candidate evaluation), not a bounded classification-rule fix like the fused-diazine cluster.
mechanism: Each of the two ortho-fused rings independently gets an ODD Pass-1 pi-electron count when evaluated as its own SSSR ring (every ring atom contributes 1pi via an endo- or exocyclic-to-carbon double bond, so an odd-membered evaluation set is structurally guaranteed to sum odd). Neither ring reaches Aromatic (4n+2) or Antiaromatic (4n), so Pass 2 never seeds (seeding requires an ALREADY-aromatic adjacent ring). This is a genuine per-ring-evaluation blind spot, not a misclassified rule: azulene's real 10pi system is a non-alternant, whole-perimeter delocalized system that no single SSSR ring, evaluated alone, can ever see -- unlike the fused-diazine cluster, there is no single branch of one rule to correct here.
contrast_with_fused_diazine_fix: The fused-diazine fix corrected one branch of one carbon rule (CarbonExocyclicHeteroatomDouble), with a fully-reasoned, empirically-verified, bounded blast radius (5000-molecule corpus, 0 new mismatches in either convention). This cluster has no analogous single-rule target -- the defect is architectural (per-ring evaluation, not per-atom rule content).

evidence.default_engine_vs_rdkit_on_49_cluster_mo: 0/49 match RDKit (matches the original K2b diagnosis exactly)
evidence.existing_experimental_engine_vs_rdkit_on: 49/49 match RDKit, 0 kekulize/internal-invariant errors -- verified two independent ways: (1) a throwaway probe calling the public apply_aromaticity_rdkit_parity_experimental API directly (then deleted, not committed -- duplicated existing capability), (2) the project's own pre-existing crates/chematic-perception/examples/rdkit_parity_full_corpus.rs diagnostic, run against scripts/descriptor_census_corpus.smi and joined against a live rdkit==2026.03.3 oracle at set level (not a count comparison): 4976/4978 comparable molecules match (99.9956% atom-level agreement); the only 2 mismatches are unrelated giant fullerene-cage molecules (75+ fused rings), not azulene-type; all 49 azulene-cluster molecules are in the matching set (0 overlap with the 2 mismatches).

why_the_existing_experimental_engine_is_: apply_aromaticity_rdkit_parity_experimental / assign_aromaticity_rdkit_parity_experimental (crates/chematic-perception/src/rdkit_parity.rs, landed in Aromaticity-A1-1b-0/A1-1b-1, docs/aromaticity_a1_rfc.md) already exists in-tree, already gives 100.0000%/99.9956% RDKit atom-flag agreement on two independently-run 5000-molecule corpora, and already resolves all 49 of this cluster's molecules. But it is architecturally different from the production Huckel Pass-1/Pass-2 model: RDKit-style GLOBAL per-molecule electron-donor typing (a bond only counts toward an atom's donor type if it lies on ANY SSSR ring in the whole molecule, ported from RDKit's real getAtomDonorTypeArom/applyHuckelToFused) plus enumeration of connected fused-ring SUBSETS (size 1..=6, RDKit's own maxNumFusedRings cap) with Huckel applied per subset -- not a rule inside the existing per-SSSR-ring ring_pi_electrons. Routing apply_aromaticity()'s default through it, or adding it as a new AromaticityAlgorithm variant, is explicitly what this PR's hard constraints forbid, and is exactly the step the RFC itself flags as needing "a fresh explicit go-ahead" that has not been given ([aromaticity_a1_rfc.md] A1-1b-0: "the gate being met (and exceeded) is not itself that go-ahead").
middle_path_considered_and_rejected: Wiring ONLY the A1-1a component-model's multi-ring fused-envelope candidate generation (build_conjugated_components, already in-tree, no global donor typing) into assign_aromaticity_ex's Pass 1 was considered. The A1-1a RFC section already shows this alone is sufficient to fix azulene in its diagnostic-only exhaustive_aromaticity_oracle. Rejected as a fix for THIS PR because: (1) it is a structural change to Pass 1 (a new KIND of candidate, not a bounded rule correction), not a specific-and-correctable classification mechanism; (2) candidate-widening can only ever ADD aromaticity, never remove a false positive, so it carries a real full-corpus false-positive risk (e.g. any fused bicyclic where the whole-envelope union coincidentally sums to 4n+2 even though only one ring is genuinely aromatic) that would need its own from-scratch corpus-scale verification effort comparable to what A1-1a/A1-1b originally did across multiple dedicated rounds; (3) the project already explored this direction and deliberately superseded it with the full RDKit-parity port specifically because candidate-widening alone was insufficient for the OTHER clusters (false-positive family, purine) -- both of which this PR's fused-diazine fix has since independently resolved in the default engine, but that does not retroactively make candidate-widening a validated, low-risk mechanism for azulene specifically; (4) rdkit_parity_aromaticity already solves this cluster, fully verified -- reimplementing an approximation of it a second time inside Pass 1 would duplicate already-verified work for a worse (partial, freshly-unverified) result.
strategic_implication_for_the_coordinato: The coordinator framed the fallback as (a) scope this cluster out of K2b with a narrower description, or (b) make authoritative demotion an opt-in policy instead of changing apply_aromaticity()'s default. Both remain valid. But the research surfaced a third consideration worth flagging, not deciding: apply_aromaticity_rdkit_parity_experimental already resolves not just this 49-molecule cluster but essentially the entire remaining post-fused-diazine gap (55 molecules: 49 azulene-type + 4 fused-diazine compound cases + 2 large-polycyclic) at 99.9956% corpus-wide agreement, already merged, already gated, already opt-in. Promoting it to apply_aromaticity()'s default is a bigger, separate decision (explicitly flagged in its own RFC as needing a fresh go-ahead, and forbidden by this PR's hard constraints) -- but it exists as a live option distinct from (a)/(b), and the coordinator/maintainer may want to weigh it.
files_touched_this_round_note: Zero production or test code changes. Investigation only: read docs/aromaticity_a1_rfc.md, ran the existing rdkit_parity_full_corpus.rs example against scripts/descriptor_census_corpus.smi, joined against a freshly-generated live RDKit oracle. A throwaway verification example was written and deleted (not committed).
